subject.title: feat(durable): add beta3 runtime core foundation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this durable runtime foundation and its persistent state model, environment controls, CLI, Gateway protocol, and lifecycle integrations as supported core contracts?
rationale: The patch is a broad new product and architecture surface; code review and tests can assess implementation quality but cannot authorize its permanent compatibility and operational commitments.

options.title: Sponsor after repair and proof
options.body: Approve the architecture after the concrete findings are fixed and exact-head upgrade, restart, delivery, and current-main reconciliation evidence is supplied.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Require a smaller shared-state and read-only inspection foundation while deferring worker, lifecycle, and wider protocol commitments.

options.title: Do not adopt the stack
options.body: Close the implementation stack and continue using existing task, session, and delivery owners until a narrower requirement is established.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Approve the architecture after the concrete findings are fixed and exact-head upgrade, restart, delivery, and current-main reconciliation evidence is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest sampled cross-surface owner and authored the recent adjacent durable-approvals landing on current main.
